Technique samples record process, materials, result and possible use. They turn experimentation into evidence for later design decisions.
Appliqué adds fabric shapes to a base fabric. Layered shapes can build colour, form and imagery.
Couching secures a yarn or cord on the surface. It can create controlled lines and texture without pulling the yarn through every stitch.

A production drawing clearly communicates the intended textile item. It connects design details, size, materials and technique locations.
Use real design dimensions rather than invented values. The drawing must match the student's actual planned item.
A technique key explains symbols or labels on the drawing. It helps the reader locate and understand planned processes.
